title: Account menu rows are announced using numbered identifiers
category: Screen Reader Compatibility; Content & Information Structure; Cognitive Accessibility
screen: Membership, Help and Support, Saved Addresses, Redeem Vouchers, About Us
issue: Across the sampled Account menu, speech transcription captures repeated BTN/account/service identifiers ending in numbers. The focused Membership and Saved Addresses rows do not receive their visible names in the sampled announcements. Later rows show the same pattern. This prevents reliable identification of destinations from speech alone.
expected: Each row announces its visible destination name and actionable role, for example "Membership, button" or "Saved Addresses, button".
wcag: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A); 2.5.3 Label in Name (A) - candidate failures pending semantics/settings retest.
status: Observed audio-derived barrier; standards mapping provisional
recommendation: Expose each row as one named actionable accessibility node. Use the visible localized menu text as its accessible name. Keep automation/resource IDs out of spoken names. Hide decorative icons and chevrons from independent focus where appropriate.
reproduce: Open Account; scroll to the service menu; swipe through Membership, Help and Support and Saved Addresses. Compare the announced name against each visible label.
retest: Repeat with Display speech output enabled and Speak element IDs disabled, if present. Capture the accessibility node name/role or UI hierarchy. Confirm every row is identifiable and activatable without viewing its position.
impact: A screen-reader user cannot reliably discover account actions by their names; numbered destinations require sighted interpretation or memorisation. No complete task blockage was tested.
impact_type: Analyst interpretation of potential user impact; not measured through participant testing.

title: Pickup and destination fields announce identifiers instead of useful field content
category: Screen Reader Compatibility; Forms & Input Accessibility; Maps & Location Accessibility
issue: At 09:00-09:19, transcription captures LBL/pickup and TXT/pickup/location, followed by LBL/drop and TXT/drop/location. The visible "Your Location" value and "Where are you going?" prompt are not present in these sampled announcements. The clip then reaches the add-stop control and leaves the flow.
expected: Announce the field purpose, current value or empty state, role and activation hint: e.g. "Pickup, Your Location, button" and "Destination, not set, button". Announce a resolved address when available.
wcag: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A); 2.5.3 Label in Name (A). Check 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (A) after inspecting the node tree.
status: Observed audio-derived barrier; standards mapping provisional
recommendation: Combine each field label, value and action into a coherent accessible control. Provide meaningful localized names and expose value changes. Verify address entry can be completed through a text/list alternative to map manipulation.
reproduce: Open Rides; swipe through Pickup, its displayed value, Drop and its prompt. Compare spoken output with the visible labels and values.
retest: With element-ID speech off, activate each field, enter a public pickup/destination, select a result, and return. Check speech output, focus return, updated values and errors.
impact: Users may not know what is currently selected or how to enter their route. Severity reflects the importance of route entry; the recording does not prove that entry or booking is impossible.
impact_type: Analyst interpretation of potential user impact; not measured through participant testing.

title: Home speech contains implementation identifiers and extra focus stops
category: Screen Reader Compatibility; Navigation & Interaction; Cognitive Accessibility
issue: Service controls, search and promotional content are preceded or replaced by BTN/IMG/TAB-style identifiers. In the search segment, transcription captures BTN underscore search, the visible search prompt, then IMG underscore search as a separate announcement. Some service names and tab roles are also spoken correctly. Identifier noise is observed; the exact accessibility-node structure is not available.
expected: One concise meaningful announcement for each action, with its role/state where relevant. Decorative child icons should not create redundant focus stops.
wcag: Usability observation; investigate 4.1.2 and 1.3.1. Identifier noise alone is not sufficient to declare a WCAG failure when the correct name is also exposed.
status: Observed usability issue; WCAG failure not established
recommendation: Use human-readable names for interactive controls, group icon and label into one action, and remove redundant decorative nodes. Preserve useful selected states and tab roles.
reproduce: On Home, swipe through the service tiles, destination search and first promotion. Note repeated identifiers and whether icon and text are separate stops.
retest: Disable element-ID speech if available. Repeat sequential swipes without interrupting speech; inspect node names and child focusability. Check Voice Access separately.
impact: Adds listening time and cognitive load during discovery. Useful names are spoken for some controls, so this is not a blanket screen-reader incompatibility claim.
impact_type: Analyst interpretation of potential user impact; not measured through participant testing.

title: Destination-search prompt has low rendered contrast
issue: The prompt "Where are you going?" is light grey on a light-grey field. Sampled foreground RGB 159/159/159 against background 244/244/244 gives approximately 2.41:1 in the recording.
expected: At least 4.5:1 for normal text, including an active input prompt; at least 3:1 if the text qualifies as large. This sample is below both thresholds.
wcag: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) (AA) - sampled visual evidence; final device measurement pending.
status: Measured in recording; original-image confirmation required
evidence: E06 at 01:52.5; frame_023 original coordinates: text (269,590), background (100,570); contrast_measurements.json
recommendation: Darken the prompt or change the field background. Test the active field in all supported themes and states using original screenshots/design colours.
reproduce: View Home in the recorded light appearance; inspect the destination prompt. Sample solid text interiors and adjacent background, avoiding anti-aliased edge pixels.
retest: Measure original screenshots on-device and confirm the field is active. Recheck at increased font/display size and with supported contrast settings.
impact: Users with low vision or reduced contrast sensitivity may miss the primary destination-search entry point.
impact_type: Analyst interpretation of potential user impact; not measured through participant testing.

title: White Check text has low contrast against its yellow-orange gradient
issue: The white "Check" label is displayed over a yellow-orange gradient. Three adjacent background samples at the text height yield ratios of about 1.69:1, 1.89:1, 2.12:1. These samples are below 3:1 as well as 4.5:1. The active button receives TalkBack focus in the clip.
expected: Maintain at least 4.5:1 for normal text over the background beneath all glyphs, or 3:1 for qualifying large text.
wcag: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) (AA) - sampled visual evidence; final device measurement pending.
status: Measured in recording; original-image confirmation required
evidence: E07 at 02:02.5; frame_025 original text region (426,144)-(498,171); background x=417 at y=145,155,165; contrast_measurements.json
recommendation: Use a sufficiently dark text colour or a darker button fill. Validate the full gradient under every part of the label and every state.
reproduce: Scroll Home until the Check button of the first promotion is visible. Compare white text with the gradient at its text height.
retest: Measure original screenshots/design colours across the full label. Verify pressed, focused and disabled states separately. Review descriptive action names in context.
impact: Low-vision users may struggle to read promotional action labels and identify where the card can be opened.
impact_type: Analyst interpretation of potential user impact; not measured through participant testing.
